\abstract{\textbf{Motivation:} Read mapping, genome alignment and pangenome analysis all start by finding seeds, exact matches between a query and a reference; on short reads, seeding takes 40\% to 60\% of single-threaded BWA-MEM's time. The tools that compute seeds are fragmented: each kind of seed has its own program, index and output format, and the newest kinds, frequency-capped maximal exact matches and f-SMEMs, are offered by one or two tools each. Few of these tools are built for current processors, with their wide vector units and many cores: MUMmer4, copMEM2 and minibwa's SMEM search use one core per query sequence.\\
\textbf{Results:} We present sporos, one library that computes all of these seeds exactly, on every core and vector lane. Its main algorithmic contribution counts the copies of a MEM's string from the MEMs themselves: a string occurs in the reference once for every MEM whose query interval contains its own, so frequency-capped MEMs need no index of the genomes beyond the one that finds the MEMs. On one Intel Skylake-X processor, sporos computed minimizers and syncmers 1.8--2.3 times faster than simd-minimizers on one core, looked seeds up 3.9 times faster than minimap2, found MEMs between two human chromosomes 1 2.0--2.4 times faster than copMEM2, MEMs and MUMs 4.2--43 times faster than MUMmer4 with identical output, frequency-capped MEMs 121--176 times faster than Mumemto, and SMEMs of short reads 4.8 times faster than minibwa.\\
\textbf{Availability and implementation:} sporos is free software under the MIT license, written in Mojo with C, Python and command-line interfaces, at \url{https://github.com/kokyriakidis/sporos}.}
